When you start a startup, so many people tell you to ship fast and ship messy.

"You’ll know you have PMF when people use your broken product."

I think this is outdated advice that doesn't work anymore in 2024.

Maybe better today would be: "ship fast, small scope, high quality"

Calendly didn’t have a technical co-founder

Instead, they built the product with a dev agency

(Jam too!)

There’s no one way to build a startup

Don’t let people tell you you need a technical cofounder to start your company

Best hiring advice I’ve received:

Hire people who love what they do so much, they listen to podcasts about it.

Getting to build with these people will make your day. Their obsession, their love for the craft, it’s infectious and awesome 🤩

Startup advice says: get users in asap

But pre-PMF, if users don't stay, it's hard to know why

We decided to try a new rule:

No launches until our team 100% loves using it

Building for ourselves 1st helped us find PMF

Way faster to iterate internally than wait for feedback!

PMF is a lot easier to solve if you split it into 2 steps:

Promise Market Fit: Will people buy a product with your promise?

Product Market Fit: Once they buy & sign up, do they stay?

Once you have a promise people want, keep iterating until your product fulfills the promise

10 yr old startup advice that hasn't aged well:

"If you're not embarrassed, you've shipped too late"

10 yrs ago, yes.

But today, people expect high quality, even from startups.

Startups do need to ship fast. But keep scope small enough to deliver a great 1st impression.

Great engineering teams do the boring things well:

- Internal docs
- Code organization
- Bugs & testing
- Local env
- Deployment
- Team coordination

Hard to do well, but when you do, it's so much faster and more fun to build!
